newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSIGHT - JGBs seen bullish, trying for 127.34.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - JGBs seen bullish, trying for 127.34.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract is likely to try for the all-time high for any benchmark contract of 127.34 on Wednesday as the recent firm tone is expected to continue.
The contract ended Tokyo at 127.12 on Tuesday. It rose as high as 127.23 later on LIFFE before closing there at 127.15.
Traders said the September's rise to 127.23 was mainly due to news which came late on Tuesday that medium-sized Japanese construction company Daito Kogyo Co Ltd had failed.
Some traders said the contract may rise towards 127.50 on Wednesday while others were cautious about current levels.
"The September's rise should not be blocked at 127.34," said a dealer at a city bank's securities unit, adding that he saw no major resistance point to as high as 127.50.

"The current firmness comes from buy orders at the long-end of JGB yield curve. It would be more significant if the key 182nd 10-year JGB yield slips below two percent," he said. The yield hit an all-time low of 2.060 percent on Tuesday.

But other traders said they were afraid of poor results in a forthcoming 10-year JGB auction due next week, because if the contract rises that high, the Finance Ministry may set the coupon rate at a record low 2.2 percent.
